overview: Architecture and painting show different sides of Spain's sixteenth- and seventeenth-century culture: a royal monastery organized around worship and learning, and pictures shaped by observation and international exchange.

items.text: Philip II founded El Escorial in 1563. Juan Bautista de Toledo designed the complex, and Juan de Herrera completed the work after Toledo's death.
El Escorial combined a monastery, church, palace, school, seminary and royal library around courtyards. Religious life, royal authority and study occupied one complex.
Early in his seventeenth-century career, Velazquez painted kitchen scenes known as bodegones and studied figures directly from life.
Velazquez became painter to Philip IV in 1623. Later at Madrid, Venetian paintings and contact with Rubens helped shape his art.
